subject: POC kickoff & trial checklist — multilingual model recommendation and success criteria
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example>
To: Maria Gomez <maria@linguakart.com>, Dev Ops <devops@linguakart.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.example>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-08-09T15:12:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: POC kickoff & trial checklist — multilingual model recommendation and success criteria

Hi Maria / team,

Thanks again for taking time today — great kickoff. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed POC approach, success criteria, timeline, and who owns what so we can get agreement and kick off next week. I've attached a one-page POC plan and the prompt/eval suite we'll run.

Summary of ask from your side:
- Validate assistant answers for catalog search, product Q&A, and simple transactional flows in Spanish, Portuguese, and French.
- Target latency p95 <= 300ms for single-turn queries, and correct/acceptable responses for >85% of sampled prompts (see sampling plan attached).

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) Week 0 (this week): finalize data access + test account. OWNER: LinguaKart (Maria / Dev Ops) + Redwood SE (Sergio) for access.
2) Week 1: Integration & baseline run — deploy Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized) as primary model, Mistral-7B as a fallback for lower-latency checks. Collect latency/error metrics and initial sample outputs. OWNER: Redwood (Sergio) + LinguaKart devs.
3) Week 2: Prompt tuning & multilingual evaluation — run our prompt-suite across targeted locales, gather human-inspected scores and automated metrics (exact-match intent, topical accuracy). OWNER: Redwood (Vanessa / Prioyom for eval harness).
4) Week 3: Optimize for cost/latency — try Redwood Optimize suggestions (KV caching, batching, quantization tweaks) and produce final report + go/no-go recommendation.

Success criteria (proposal):
- Latency: p95 single-turn <= 300ms on Dedicated-like instance (target 250ms).
- Quality: >= 85% acceptability across sampled prompts per locale (human eval).
- Stability: <1% error rate and no model hallucinations on a curated high-risk prompt set.
- Operations: Stable prefix/KV caching enabled and token cost within estimated range (TBD in the attached spreadsheet).

Model recommendation rationale:
- Primary: Llama-2-13B-chat (quantized) — strong instruction-following and widely compatible with Redwood serving runtime; good balance of quality and latency for your catalog scenario.
- Fallback: Mistral-7B (quantized) — used for lower-latency short-turn queries and as a fallback path when dedicated capacity is constrained.
- Multilingual handling: We'll use locale-specific prompt templates and a small reranker (embedding-based) for Spanish/Portuguese/French to improve candidate selection. If we see degradation in FR/PT, we can test a larger multilingual variant (e.g., a 30B multilingual) as a second-tier option.

Next steps I need from you (quick):
- Confirm we can create a test API key + dev access by Thursday (8/12).
- Share a sample of 200 representative prompts per locale (encrypted link or Drive).
- Confirm which metrics you care most about for the final go/no-go (latency vs. quality tradeoffs).

I'll schedule a 30-min sync for Tuesday to align infra (Sergio + your Dev Ops).

Thanks — happy to adjust if you want different models/more conservative SLAs.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.example
+1 415-555-0192

Attachments: LinguaKart_POC_plan_v1.xlsx, prompt-suite-multilingual.md

From: Maria Gomez <maria@linguakart.com>

Date: 2026-08-10T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: POC kickoff & trial checklist — multilingual model recommendation and success criteria

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks — this looks thorough and aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- We can spin up a test API key and provide network access by Friday (8/13), but Dev Ops will need the exact IP ranges and auth method to whitelist.
- For success criteria, the business is most sensitive to quality in Spanish (primary market) and overall latency for UX. If we have to pick one "must" metric it should be Spanish quality >= 88% acceptability. Latency target is fine but flexible if quality is prioritized.
- Regarding models: we prefer to avoid larger 30B models unless necessary for quality. If Llama-2-13B-chat falls short on Spanish, we're open to testing a specialized multilingual model you recommend.

We'll upload the sample prompt sets to the Drive folder you linked by Thursday EOD.

Appreciate the clear timeline — please send the IP whitelist details and the test-account template.

Best,
Maria Gomez

Hi all,

I've added the IP ranges and the test-account template to the Drive folder (link in thread). Quick notes from the infra side:
- We recommend starting with the quantized Llama-2-13B-chat on a c5-dedicated-like instance in Redwood Dedicated for the baseline. That configuration consistently hits ~200-260ms p95 in our lab for single-turn queries with KV caching enabled.
- Fallback routing to Mistral-7B will be configured for short-turn queries; we can tune the fallback threshold after the baseline run.
